name: Adaeze Elizabeth Adeteye
feedback: Strong, disciplined submission across all four deliverables. On D1 you catalogued nine of the ten planted findings with sensible OWASP classes and CWEs: SQLi (A03/CWE-89), alg:none JWT (CWE-347), hardcoded secret sankofa-legacy-admin-2019 (CWE-798), missing expiry (CWE-613), insecure cookie (CWE-614), XXE (CWE-611), stored XSS (CWE-79), open redirect (CWE-601) and path traversal (CWE-22). You missed the unsalted MD5 password hashing issue (A02/CWE-916), which is one of the core five, and that costs a finding. Your decoy call is correct and well argued: you named the hand-rolled base64url construct as the safe one and proved it is just padding correction with no exec or auth-bypass path, and you correctly did NOT label alg:none the decoy. The reason D1 is not higher is evidence: you described the vulnerable constructs but did not quote the specific line numbers or anchor findings to the capture timestamps, so several rows read as label-plus-prose rather than label-plus-quoted-line. On D2 your PoC payloads are excellent and verbatim, including the URL-encoded SQLi string and the decoded alg:none token, and your CVSS vector strings are complete with justification. Two issues hold D2 back: your chain is five hops and omits the stored XSS and open-redirect hops, and crucially you reconciled nothing to the capture log timeline (recon 02:14:08, SQLi 02:15:31, XSS 02:18:47, redirect 02:21:13, file read 02:24:02), which the key requires. Your SEC-01 SQLi vector uses A:H, but the bypass does not touch availability so it should be A:N giving roughly 9.1, not 9.8. Your impact says up to a Million naira per record; the sample shows balances up to about 950k summing to tens of millions across 312 customers tied to the BoltCash launch, and stating that running total with your assumptions would have earned the full impact mark. You also missed the senior insight that the forged super_admin token reaches the shared /api/v1/internal service, a scope change to S:C. D3 is your strongest piece: clean threat model, findings tied to evidence files, the decoy stated correctly, an earliest-break fix that removes alg:none first, remediation genuinely ordered by EFFORT rather than CVSS severity, and two detection stopgaps with exact fields (ARGS:username and legacy_admin_jwt) and real false-positive rates. The one gap is that your executive summary ends on system access rather than on a customers-and-naira headline, which is what a non-technical sponsor needs to read first. D4 is excellent: you answer all four prompts in your own voice, cite ISC2 Canons 2 and 3 by number in a load-bearing way, and tie NDPA 2023 Section 40 (72-hour NDPC notification) to the 312 affected customers; adding Section 41 (notifying data subjects on high risk) would have completed it. The single most important fix is to reconcile every exploit hop to its exact capture timestamp and include all six attack hops, because an unreconciled chain is the difference between a narrative and a proof.
